readthrough_map_scope: Reported identities in Roy et al. human/yeast reporter experiments involving ataluren and aminoglycosides. Used as a conservative non-native-product warning, not an exhaustive rule for every drug or gene.

gate_reasons.causal_variant: Confirm variant call, population frequency, inheritance/phase, transcript and causal BUB1B mechanism before translating this branch.
gate_reasons.allele_resolved_rna: Measure stop-allele RNA abundance, splicing, NMD response and the missense allele independently.
gate_reasons.protein_identity_and_function: Sequence the readthrough product and test BUBR1 function; full length or greater abundance alone is insufficient.
gate_reasons.division_normalized_rescue: Demonstrate fewer segregation errors per completed mitosis, independent of cytostasis, selective death or reporter artifacts.
gate_reasons.normal_vs_tumor_effect: Compare corrected and variant nonmalignant cells with a separately evaluated relevant tumor model; exclude abnormal-clone expansion or protection of malignant cells.
gate_reasons.exposure_feasibility: Measure intracellular target engagement at a formulation-relevant exposure, with viability and renal/hearing or other candidate-specific safety boundaries. No exposure bridge exists here.

bubr1_function.title: Suijkerbuijk et al. Molecular Causes for BUBR1 Dysfunction in MVA (2010)
bubr1_function.supports: Patient-cell checkpoint rescue with BUBR1 expression; allele-specific functional and stability defects, not proof that this case's missense is unstable.

nmd_rule.title: Zhang et al. Intron function in beta-globin nonsense-mediated decay (1998)
nmd_rule.supports: Human beta-globin experiments establish positional final-junction dependence. The module uses a conservative >55 nt boundary, with explicit exceptions.

nmd_exceptions.title: Lindeboom et al. The impact of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay on genetic disease (2019)
nmd_exceptions.supports: Start-proximal and long-exon contexts can escape NMD. The module downgrades these predictions to uncertain, without assuming measured escape.

readthrough_identity.title: Roy et al. Ataluren stimulates near-cognate tRNA selection (2016)
readthrough_identity.supports: Human/yeast reporter and CFTR readthrough studies identify non-native amino-acid insertion and context dependence; no BUB1B allele-specific insertion frequencies.

gentamicin_dmd.title: Malik et al. Gentamicin readthrough in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (2010)
gentamicin_dmd.supports: Small human DMD study measured heterogeneous dystrophin increase; not MVA efficacy or evidence of safe chronic use in this case.

gentamicin_fda.title: Drugs@FDA gentamicin ANDA 062366 current product record
gentamicin_fda.supports: Current prescription injectable products; original approval 1983, later labeling supplements.

gentamicin_label.title: DailyMed gentamicin injection prescribing information
gentamicin_label.supports: Serious susceptible bacterial-infection indications; renal clearance, renal/ototoxicity and neuromuscular concerns.

macrolide_study.title: Caspi et al. Macrolide nonsense-readthrough reporter study (2016)
macrolide_study.supports: Macrolide activity in mammalian reporter/disease systems and a mouse model; no MVA or BUB1B experiment. Full experimental details require paper/supplement review before laboratory replication.

macrolide_erratum.title: Caspi et al. Published erratum (2016)
macrolide_erratum.supports: Erratum is recorded and must accompany the original article; no assumption that an unreviewed correction validates efficacy.
macrolide_erratum.access_note: Publisher erratum endpoint did not return body; indexed author-uploaded erratum text identifies author-name corrections. PubMed verifies erratum linkage.

pcd_context.title: Properties of non-aminoglycoside readthrough compounds in PCD (2021)
pcd_context.supports: Modest, context-dependent HEK293 reporter responses and healthy nasal-cell safety assays; reporter normalization artifacts discussed. Literature's ataluren FDA-approval wording is not used: current status comes from regulators.

azithromycin_fda.title: Drugs@FDA ZITHROMAX oral suspension NDA 050710
azithromycin_fda.supports: Current prescription oral suspension; labeling supplement dated July 13, 2026.

azithromycin_label.title: FDA ZITHROMAX label revised July 2026
azithromycin_label.supports: Susceptible bacterial infections; QT, hepatotoxicity and other labeled warnings; approval does not establish genetic rescue.

amikacin_rat.title: G542X CFTR rat model sensitive to NMD (2020)
amikacin_rat.supports: Amikacin failed to restore specific CFTR function in an endogenous rat model, demonstrating transcript and model limitations.

readthrough_nmd.title: Readthrough and NMD inhibition in murine cystic fibrosis (2021)
readthrough_nmd.supports: SMG1 inhibition potentiated selected aminoglycosides including gentamicin in CF organoids; amikacin did not rescue. Unapproved NMD inhibitor is a comparator, not a recommended combination.

amikacin_fda.title: FDA amikacin ANDA 205605 approval letter (2015)
amikacin_fda.supports: FDA approval of injectable amikacin; current marketed labeling separately documented.

amikacin_label.title: DailyMed amikacin injection prescribing information
amikacin_label.supports: US prescription injection, serious bacterial infection indications, renal clearance and renal/hearing/neuromuscular warnings.

amlexanox_cells.title: Amlexanox readthrough in COL7A1 patient-derived cells (2017)
amlexanox_cells.supports: Response in 8 of 12 tested nonsense alleles; protein production and skin localization are gene/cell-specific evidence.

amlexanox_nmd.title: Gonzalez-Hilarion et al. Rescue by amlexanox in human cells (2012)
amlexanox_nmd.supports: Cell-model readthrough/NMD observations; no BUB1B rescue evidence.

amlexanox_fda.title: Drugs@FDA APHTHASOL NDA 020511
amlexanox_fda.supports: 1996 approval of dental paste; current marketing status Discontinued. Discontinuation alone does not establish safety withdrawal.

amlexanox_history.title: FDA amlexanox original application review (1996)
amlexanox_history.supports: Historical Japanese tablet approvals for asthma/rhinitis, not proof of current Japanese authorization or availability.

ataluren_ema.title: EMA Translarna authorization record
ataluren_ema.supports: European Commission non-renewal March 28, 2025 after efficacy was not confirmed; EU authorization expired. Other jurisdictions not adjudicated.

sirt2_bubr1.title: North et al. SIRT2 stabilizes BubR1 (2014)
sirt2_bubr1.supports: SIRT2/K668 stability pathway; NMN increased mouse BubR1 abundance. Lifespan experiment used genetic SIRT2 overexpression. Nicotinamide reduced BubR1 in cited cell experiments.

candidates.name: Azithromycin
candidates.mechanism: Macrolide stop-bypass probe for an experimentally confirmed nonsense substrate. The molecular route and residue insertion must be demonstrated in the BUB1B context.
candidates.study_context: Caspi et al. reported macrolide readthrough in mammalian systems and a mouse model. A separate PCD study found mostly modest reporter effects, with responses dependent on codon/context; these were not BUB1B experiments. The original paper has a linked erratum.
candidates.counter_evidence: The PCD work used HEK293 reporters, not endogenous BUB1B rescue; non-TGA reporter responses and normalization artifacts undermine generalization. Healthy nasal-cell viability does not establish safety in kidney, growing tissues or cancer. No MVA functional rescue is established.
candidates.exposure: An approved oral formulation makes a formulation bridge more plausible than a discontinued topical product, but free cytosolic concentration at a translating BUB1B ribosome is unmeasured. Tissue accumulation cannot stand in for that measurement. QT prolongation, liver injury and antibacterial resistance remain constraints; no safe chronic rescue exposure is established.
candidates.tumor_normal: Hypothesis: restore chromosome segregation in nonmalignant variant cells. Test malignant cells separately: neither antitumor macrolide observations nor normal-cell rescue predict effects on tumor fitness, clonal selection or concurrent anticancer agents.
candidates.falsification: Drop if endogenous full-length BUBR1 and per-division segregation do not improve at exposure-compatible noncytotoxic conditions, if signal is restricted to a reporter, or if malignant/aneuploid clones gain a survival advantage.

approval.indication: Specified susceptible bacterial infections under population-specific labeling
approval.qualification: Current prescription formulation verified; no approval for MVA or nonsense rescue.

phenotype_reasons.cancer: Locally documented cancer makes separate tumor-versus-normal-cell effects an unresolved gate.

candidates.name: Gentamicin
candidates.mechanism: Aminoglycoside premature-stop readthrough probe; residual stop-allele mRNA and a functional inserted residue are required.
candidates.study_context: A small DMD human study showed heterogeneous dystrophin increases after treatment. This supports a human stop-bypass mechanism, not benefit in MVA. CF organoid experiments separately show that transcript depletion can limit readthrough.
candidates.counter_evidence: No BUB1B rescue is established. Aminoglycoside uptake and stop context are limiting; a full-length product can carry a damaging non-native residue. Broader translational effects and selective cell death can imitate correction.
candidates.exposure: US injectable antibacterial formulation is approved. Predominantly extracellular distribution and renal clearance do not establish effective cytosolic BUB1B exposure. Nephrotoxicity, often irreversible ototoxicity and neuromuscular effects strongly constrain prolonged investigation; no acceptable case-specific exposure margin is shown.
candidates.tumor_normal: Assess corrected and variant nonmalignant cells, kidney-relevant cells and malignant cells independently. Killing abnormal cells can lower measured aneuploidy without restoring segregation; improved tumor-cell fitness would contradict a favorable rescue interpretation.
candidates.falsification: Reject translation if functional rescue requires exposure inconsistent with a credible renal/hearing safety margin, if RNA substrate is absent, or if restored protein lacks checkpoint function. Do not infer rescue from surviving-cell counts.

approval.qualification: Current prescription injection verified; no MVA or readthrough indication.

phenotype_reasons.kidney: The local kidney feature heightens a labeled renal-toxicity concern; it does not prove reduced renal function.
phenotype_reasons.growth: Local growth/muscle concerns increase the importance of viability and neuromuscular evaluation; no neuromuscular disorder is inferred.
phenotype_reasons.cancer: Normal-cell repair and tumor-cell fitness require separate evaluation.

candidates.name: Amikacin
candidates.mechanism: Lower-priority aminoglycoside comparator testing whether another approved compound performs differently at the same stop context.
candidates.study_context: An endogenous G542X CFTR rat study found no significant specific functional rescue with amikacin. A mouse organoid study found NMD-inhibitor synergy with some aminoglycosides, but not amikacin. These are informative negative controls for a class-wide rescue assumption.
candidates.counter_evidence: Negative endogenous-gene data place this below gentamicin despite antibacterial approval. Similar-class membership supplies no positive BUB1B efficacy evidence.
candidates.exposure: Approved injectable antibacterial, with renal clearance and renal/ototoxicity warnings. Existing tissue exposure does not prove ribosomal target engagement or acceptable long-term margin for this purpose. Inhaled liposomal amikacin is a different formulation and is not used as evidence for systemic rescue.
candidates.tumor_normal: Same per-division and clonal-selection controls as gentamicin; toxicity in nonmalignant cells cannot be relabeled as beneficial antitumor action.
candidates.falsification: Do not advance without direct endogenous BUB1B functional rescue exceeding gentamicin or resolving a measured exposure limitation; stop on kidney-relevant toxicity or altered malignant-clone fitness.

approval.qualification: FDA approval letter plus current US prescription labeling documented; no MVA indication or long-term rescue safety established.

phenotype_reasons.kidney: Local kidney feature triggers the renal-liability penalty without assuming impaired renal clearance.
phenotype_reasons.growth: Local growth/muscle features require direct viability and neuromuscular assessment.
phenotype_reasons.cancer: Separate malignant and nonmalignant effects remain unmeasured.

candidates.name: Amlexanox (mechanistic comparator)
candidates.mechanism: Combined readthrough/NMD modulation could address both premature termination and loss of RNA substrate; this is conditional on measured allele-level NMD.
candidates.study_context: Human-cell studies reported transcript and full-length-protein recovery; COL7A1 patient-derived cells responded for 8 of 12 tested nonsense alleles. These are distinct disorders and provide no BUB1B rescue result.
candidates.counter_evidence: Response varied across cells/alleles. NMD modulation could increase truncated products or alter other transcripts. No approved systemic exposure bridge is verified; historical US approval cannot establish a current systemic drug option.
candidates.exposure: US APHTHASOL dental paste is listed discontinued. The original FDA review notes historic Japanese tablet approvals, but current Japanese authorization and availability were not verified. Topical oral-ulcer exposure is not a systemic BUB1B exposure rationale.
candidates.tumor_normal: Measure truncated and full-length products plus malignant-clone behavior. Broad RNA-surveillance effects must be distinguished from intended single-allele rescue; antitumor observations elsewhere do not predict benefit here.
candidates.falsification: Exclude from approved-medication shortlist unless a current medicinal formulation/jurisdiction is verified; discard the mechanism if increased RNA only increases truncated protein, without division-normalized rescue.

approval.jurisdiction: United States; Japanese historical evidence only
approval.formulation: APHTHASOL dental paste (historical US); historic Japanese tablets
approval.qualification: US marketing discontinued; not claimed to be a safety withdrawal. Current marketed systemic approval remains unverified.

candidates.name: Ataluren (regulatory exclusion comparator)
candidates.mechanism: Stop-bypass comparator useful for orthogonal readthrough/product-identity experiments; former approval must not be treated as current EU approval.
candidates.study_context: Reporter and CFTR studies identified near-cognate residue insertion. This helps define protein-identity controls; it does not establish BUB1B rescue.
candidates.counter_evidence: EU authorization was not renewed after efficacy was not confirmed. Positive reporters are insufficient to establish clinical benefit, and the published PCD study also showed modest/context-dependent responses.
candidates.exposure: No current approved formulation meeting this screen's verified-jurisdiction criterion. Research use, historical authorization and approvals claimed in older papers do not meet that gate.
candidates.tumor_normal: Any experimental protein increase must be accompanied by normal-cell functional rescue and absence of tumor or aneuploid-clone growth advantage.
candidates.falsification: Exclude from the approved shortlist on documented EU expiry; reassess only with independently verified current authorization elsewhere and an exposure bridge, never an old paper's approval claim.

approval.qualification: European Commission non-renewal March 28, 2025; no current approval in another jurisdiction verified in this ledger.

candidates.name: NMN / SIRT2 stabilization (research comparator)
candidates.mechanism: Test residual-functional-BUBR1 stabilization only if the missense allele is experimentally shown to retain function and undergo excess turnover.
candidates.study_context: SIRT2-dependent K668 deacetylation stabilized BubR1; NMN raised mouse protein abundance. Genetic SIRT2 overexpression supplied lifespan evidence, not an NMN clinical trial. MVA experiments show that some other BUBR1 alleles are unstable.
candidates.counter_evidence: Neither local missense instability nor retained function is established. A nearby published allele is not evidence for this allele. Increasing a defective protein can fail despite abundance rescue; this approach cannot replace a missing C-terminal region.
candidates.exposure: No approved medicinal NMN or selective SIRT2-activator formulation is verified. Supplement availability is not drug approval. Do not substitute nicotinamide: it reduced BubR1 abundance in the cited cellular experiments.
candidates.tumor_normal: Require allele-specific half-life, K668 target engagement and chromosome-fidelity rescue in nonmalignant cells while monitoring separately for changed tumor fitness; altered proliferation alone is not success.
candidates.falsification: Drop stabilization if the missense protein is stable but dysfunctional, if increased abundance fails to restore segregation, or if harmful clones are preserved. Keep outside approved shortlist absent regulatory evidence.

approval.qualification: No verified approved medicine; mechanistic comparator only.

experiment_sequence: Validate the two calls independently, resolve phase and population frequencies, and verify the expressed transcript. Compare variant cells with isogenic correction and matched nonmalignant controls. A cis result revises the two-allele causal model before drug claims.

Measure allele-specific RNA, splicing and protein with N- and C-terminal assays. Use an NMD perturbation only as a mechanistic control. Choose readthrough if a verified stop substrate remains; choose stabilization only if the missense protein retains function but is unstable.

Screen the approved probes separately, using the allele's endogenous sequence and intron-containing context. Add reporter-free full-length immunoblot/proteomics and sequence the inserted residue. Intronless cDNA alone cannot test NMD. Include vehicle, corrected cells, genetic BUB1B rescue, and short-lived reporter/cell-count controls.

Predefine primary function as segregation error frequency per completed division from blinded live-cell lineages. Also measure checkpoint arrest/release, kinetochore attachment, micronuclei, viable yield and cell-cycle duration across independent biological replicates. Require concordant protein and functional rescue; no invented success threshold substitutes for observed variance/power planning.

Compare nonmalignant, kidney-relevant and separately established malignant models. Track karyotype and clone abundance longitudinally. Reject apparent correction caused by selective death, slower cycling, checkpoint bypass, or expansion/protection of abnormal clones.

Measure intracellular exposure, target engagement and washout durability against formulation-relevant pharmacology. If rescue occurs only without a credible exposure margin, retain a mechanistic finding and stop clinical translation. No dose or treatment recommendation is produced.
comparison_claim: The competitive advantage is a falsifiable causal chain: variant to transcript availability to protein identity to mitotic fidelity, with explicit approval and exposure gates. Unlike the first pass's downstream stress hypotheses, this can distinguish three competing mechanisms in the same cells. It is a stronger experimental design, not evidence of a better treatment or a higher probability of winning. Negative results remain informative: an NMD-depleted transcript, a nonfunctional inserted residue, or a stable-but-defective missense protein each rejects a different branch.
